Continuation of the character-to-colour lookup beginning at $7FCF; this byte is entry $31 of that table, and entries continue through $80CE.

A 256-byte table of bottom-right character codes indexed by a metatile value. The resident draw loop at $6D60 writes the selected code one row below and one cell to the right of the first cell.

Write $46 plus 1 modulo 256 to $B23E and $B288, set sound state $2C15 to 2, and use stage index $7B to format fields $4783,X and $4789,X through $AF42 for destination selectors $9B and $AF. The formatter’s display callback was stubbed in the controlled checks.

Save X and Y in immediate operands, call $36E9 to split A into nibbles plus one, clear the first two bytes at $B283, and write the tens and units codes to the next two bytes. The incoming processor flags select the path: negative enters the first-price balance check at $AF9E; zero selects a message at $AFEC; otherwise use the second-price path at $AF70. The controlled cases set these flags directly, so ordinary-play choice mapping remains open.

Call $78D1 with stage field $4789,X, where X comes from $7B. Reload X and read callback high byte $4771,X. Load a message pointer from this entry, set A=4 and enter $AFDC; that path calls $77E0 and restores A before adding to the meter. The controlled tests stubbed the message routine.

If selected-player high balance $4DC7,Y is zero and low balance $4DC9,Y is less than stage field $4783,X under an unsigned byte comparison, jump to $B0DC. Otherwise continue to the first-price payment at $AFB3.

Call $78D1 with stage field $4783,X and reload stage index. If callback high byte $477D,X is nonzero, patch the JSR from $4777/$477D, clear that high byte and call the target; then use A=8 at $AFE1. Otherwise enter the message path at $AFD6. Payment and callback effects were stubbed.
Load a message pointer from this entry, set A=8 and enter $AFDC; that path calls $77E0 and restores A before adding to the meter. The controlled tests stubbed the message routine.
Push A, call $77E0 with the selected message pointer and pull A. Continue at $AFE1; the message routine was stubbed.
Call $77A9 with A=4 or A=8, reload stage index, decrement $4753,X and jump to $B1CC. The meter callback and destination effects were not exercised in these controlled checks.
Load the message pointer encoded here and jump to $B1C9. This branch was reached by forcing the incoming zero flag.
Reload stage index, decrement $4753,X, load the message pointer encoded here and jump to $B1C9. Its ordinary caller was not exercised by the choice tests.
Store zero at $B288, set sound state $2C15 to 2, and set $4D69 to 7. Reload stage index from $7B and continue to the item-pair selection. The later drawing paths start at $B04D and are separate.

Read $476B,X. If nonzero, pass it and $4771,X separately through the conditional-item resolver at $B1D8; store the returned values at $B28E/$B28F, then jump to $B04D. Four forced VICE inputs per load checked this and the implicit path with the real resolver.

Use $4771,X as Y. Clear carry, add selected-player index $4DBD to A, then add $D5 with the carry from that first addition. Patch this as the low byte of an absolute read; load $4D and add the carry from the second addition to form its high byte. Index values and carry behavior are not locally bounded.

Read the patched absolute address, clear carry and add $B290,Y. Store the result at $B28E, then store that result plus one modulo 256 at $B28F. Continue at $B04D; the later drawing callbacks were not exercised.

Load the second selected item byte at $B28F, multiply it by eight modulo 256 and read a target pointer from the table at $B5E1. Patch the JSR operand at $B063/$B064. The item index is not locally bounded.

Multiply A by 8 with three eight-bit shifts and use the result as Y. Copy bytes at $B5E1,Y and $B5E2,Y into the operand of the JSR at $B062. Controlled inputs 0–23 select the captured pointer pairs; no local index bound is enforced. The target routines and natural-play contexts remain open.

Call the patched target with A=$E4. Then read the first item byte at $B28E, multiply it by eight modulo 256 and patch a second JSR from the same pointer table. Controlled checks replaced both selected targets with logging stubs; actual drawing effects remain separate.

Multiply A by 8 with three eight-bit shifts and use the result as Y. Copy bytes at $B5E1,Y and $B5E2,Y into the operand of the JSR at $B07A. Controlled inputs 0–23 select the captured pointer pairs; no local index bound is enforced. The target routines and natural-play contexts remain open.
Call the second patched target with A=$D0, then set the temporary row counter at $B5DE to 3 and begin filling colour RAM. The target was replaced with a logging stub in the controlled checks.

For each of three rows, write colour 9 to four bytes at $D8F8,Y and four at $D90C,Y. Y starts at zero and advances by 40 after each row; the counter at $B5DE ends at zero. With I/O visible, these are colour RAM writes. The next setup continues at $B09C.

Store $46 plus one modulo 256 at $B23E. Pass the first selected item at $B28E to $B245, then call $B22A with Y=$73. Repeat for the second item at $B28F with Y=$87. The format and display callbacks were stubbed in the controlled tests.

Call $77E0 with the message pointer selected by the preceding path, then fall through to the mode and countdown initializer at $B0BF. The ordinary label path loads $B295; earlier branches can supply other pointers. The message callback was stubbed in the controlled tests.

Store 0 in the shop mode byte at $B289, store $DC in the countdown at $B28D, and fall through to the wait path at $B0C9. Starting from 0, the captured left and right handlers keep the mode among $FF, $00 and $01 if no other code changes it; ordinary-play timing and other possible writes remain open.

Call $3C2A, decrement the shop countdown at $B28D and branch to $B0FC when it becomes zero. Otherwise call $370B, $B200 and $B1ED; on set carry, repeat this path. On clear carry, fall through to $B0DC. Starting from the initialized $DC and holding the tested branches, zero is reached after 220 calls to $3C2A. In the forced load-2 play snapshot, VICE measured 12,969,296 cycles (about 13.16 seconds at the PAL 985,248 Hz clock) for each controlled wait branch, with $5275=1, real interrupts and the other shop callbacks stubbed. Normal-play timing remains open.

Call $3C2A, decrement $B28D and branch to $B0FC at zero. Otherwise call $370B, $B200 and $3C4C, then fall through to the sampled-input choice at $B0ED. The controlled test stubs these calls; normal-play timing and other exits remain open.

Use the sampled active-low inputs: if $70 is zero, branch to the shop gate at $B150; otherwise, if $73 is zero, branch to the left handler at $B112; otherwise, if $74 is zero, branch to the right handler at $B130. When all three are nonzero, jump back to $B0DC. The preceding code calls $3C4C to sample joystick port 2; fire takes priority over left, and left over right.

If $B288 is nonzero, jump to $AFF3. Otherwise load X from $7B, store $FF at $4753,X, load X/Y with message pointer $B2CA, and jump to the $77E0 call at $B1C9. The selector used by $77E0 and natural timeout reachability remain open.

If the signed mode byte at $B289 is negative, return to the wait path at $B0C9. Otherwise decrement it with eight-bit wrap. If the new value is nonzero and $B288 is zero, pass the item index at $B28E to the message selector at $B218. Call $B200 and return to the wait path. If the mode byte at $B289 equals 1, return to the wait path at $B0C9. Otherwise increment it with eight-bit wrap. If the new value is nonzero and $B288 is zero, pass the item index at $B28F to the message selector at $B218. Call $B200 and return to the wait path. Read $B288; if nonzero, load $B289 and jump to $AF6C. Otherwise load X from $7B and read $B289. If nonzero, branch to the purchase index choice at $B179, preserving the negative flag from that read. Choose an item index using the incoming negative flag: load $B28E when it is set, or $B28F when clear, then enter the price selector at $B184. The path at $B150 supplies that flag from $B289; other entries remain open.

Multiply A by 8 with three eight-bit shifts, use the result as Y, and copy the two bytes at $B5DF,Y and $B5E0,Y to $7D/$7E. Multiply A by 8 with three eight-bit shifts and use the result as Y. Copy bytes at $B5E3,Y and $B5E4,Y into the operand of the JSR at $B1C2. Controlled inputs 0–23 select the captured pointer pairs; no local index bound is enforced. The target routines and natural-play contexts remain open.

Pull the selected item index, clear carry, add 1 in binary mode and call the JSR whose operand was patched by the selector.
